methodology: The decomposition process involved analyzing both the original research topic and the generated technical specification to extract independent and self-contained atomic units. Each unit was evaluated for technical specificity and clarity to ensure it could be implemented as a single requirement. The original research topic was broken down into distinct functional requirements, while the generated specification was analyzed for its logical structure and behavior descriptions. This systematic approach ensured that all relevant aspects of the timer's functionality were captured in both sets.
mindtraced_atomic_units: The timer is started when the pattern 1101 is detected.
The timer shifts in 4 more bits to determine the duration to delay.
The timer waits for the counters to finish counting.
The timer notifies the user when it has timed out.
The timer waits for the user to acknowledge the timeout before resetting.
The state machine has an active high synchronous reset.
The state machine begins searching for the input sequence 1101 after a reset.
spec_atomic_units: The module implements a finite-state machine (FSM) that controls a timer based on the detection of the pattern 1101.
The FSM manages timing and state transitions for shifting, counting, and notifying the user.
The module has input ports: clk, reset, data, and output ports: shift_ena, counting, done.
The shift_ena signal is asserted for 4 clock cycles after detecting the pattern 1101.
The counting signal is asserted when waiting for the counters to finish counting.
The done signal is asserted when the timer times out.
The FSM waits for the ack signal to reset.
The FSM transitions occur on the positive edge of the clk signal.
The reset signal initializes the FSM to the IDLE state.
The FSM has states for IDLE, S1, S2, S3 (for pattern detection), SHIFT, COUNTING, and DONE.
Non-blocking assignments are used for state updates on the clock edge.
